Sophie: Customer t-acme reports monthly bucket dropped to 0 mid-stream; UI showed refill then API returned 429s for several minutes.
Jordan: Can you share a request id, sample curl and the exact 429 body? Also tenant timezone?
Sophie: tenant tz = America/Los_Angeles. Sample curl + headers:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abc" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-base","input":"..."}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
429 response: `{"error":"quota_exhausted","retry_after":null}`
Sophie: In logs refill write at 2026-04-15T07:59:58-07:00, UI refresh at 07:59:59, but API nodes continued returning 429 until ~08:03:20.
QuotaBot: [automated] tenant=t-acme monthly_quota=0 event_ts=2026-04-15T14:59:58Z
Maya: Sounds like a cache/invalidation race. API nodes use per-node in-memory quota cache (30s TTL) plus we keep a Redis negative cache for heavy tenants (~2m TTL). The storefront reads DB directly, so UI can reflect the refill immediately while API still has stale zero in cache.
Jordan: Why such a long gap in this case? TTLs are shorter than the observed gap.
Samir: Two contributors: kafka consumer lag (~45s) delaying invalidation fanout, and a GC pause on the refill worker that delayed the DB write acknowledgement. Combined with the Redis negative cache we saw ~3m of divergence.
Maya: Repro steps for support: (1) add tenant to heavy-tenants; (2) set monthly bucket to 0; (3) trigger refill job but pause kafka consumer/invalidation for 60-120s; (4) issue streaming requests from a cached API node -> UI shows credits but API 429s.
Sophie: Customer needs immediate workaround. Can we force cache invalidation?
Maya: I ran the admin command: `admin quota invalidate --tenant t-acme --cluster prod`. After ~10s API nodes accepted requests again. Created infra ticket INF-10234 to implement a fast-path invalidate on monthly refill and to stop using the negative-cache for refill events.
Samir: I also manually bumped tenant ledger by +120 credits and filed billing note CASE-2026-042. Customer confirms streaming resumed ~12s after our actions.
Jordan: Short-term: manual invalidate + billing adjust. Long-term: add a guaranteed invalidation publish on refill and remove Redis negative-cache from the monthly-refill path.
Sophie: Passed the workaround to the customer; they verified streaming resumed. Closing the loop. :thumbsup:
Ops: reaction :white_check_mark:
